title: Function Parameters
concept: Functions can accept multiple parameters — each with its own name and type — to receive all the data they need.
why: Most functions need more than one input. Multiple parameters let you pass all necessary data in a single call.
tips: Parameters are like function-specific variables — they only exist inside the function
The order of arguments in a call must match the order of parameters
Each parameter needs its OWN type annotation: `(x: Int, y: Int)` not `(x, y: Int)`
Give parameters descriptive names: `width` and `height` not `a` and `b`
common_mistakes: Forgetting the type on each parameter: `(x, y: Int)` only types y
Passing the wrong type: `add("5", 3)` when it expects Int, Int
